newsitem.title: USA: CSW Q4 earnings seen hurt by cool weather.
newsitem.headline: CSW Q4 earnings seen hurt by cool weather.

text.p: Cooler weather that held down Central and South West Corp's earnings in the third quarter will reduce fourth-quarter profits as well, director of investor relations Sharon R. Peavy told Reuters Thursday.
Peavy said he thought the First Call consensus estimate of $0.41 for the company's fourth quarter was "not that far off."

The utility holding company earlier said third-quarter earnings per share fell to $0.90 from $1.04 in the same period last year. The result was well below the First Call consensus estimate of $0.97. The decline reflected accounting changes and the weather, it said.
Below-normal temperatures in September would show up in October bills, she said. Undisclosed restructuring charges are also expected in the fourth quarter.

The third-quarter decline in profits also reflected increased depreciation and amortization, higher operations and maintenance costs and the loss of earnings from Transok, a natural gas pipeline sold in June 1996.

Peavy said the company also lost what it called Mirror CWIP, a non-cash addition to earnings reflecting deferred construction costs by its Central Power and Light subsidiary. Mirror CWIP added $41 million to earnings in 1995.

Those factors were partially offset by the addition of earnings from CSW's Seeboard subsidiary in Britain and higher net electric revenue, which resulted from customer growth. Still, mild weather limited the growth of net electric revenue.

In the third quarter, cooling-degree days for CSW's U.S. utilities were 6 percent less than normal and 12 percent lower than in the third quarter of 1995. CSW's U.S. utilities experience their strongest sales during the summer months, it noted.
In contrast, Seeboard has its highest sales during the winter months. Its acquisition, completed in 1996, will modify the seasonality of CSW's earnings, the company said.
